html:
A Royal Navy squadron based at Freetown from 1808 to 1867 that hunted slave ships off West Africa after Britain banned the slave trade in 1807.

It captured about 1,600 ships and freed some 150,000 Africans. Courts in Freetown judged the captured ships, and most of the freed people, called recaptives or liberated Africans, were settled in villages around the town. They came from all over West and Central Africa, many Yoruba and Igbo, and joined the older settlers to form the Krio people. Many sailors died of fever. Patrols were often weak, and millions were still shipped to Brazil and Cuba in these years.
sum: A Royal Navy squadron based at Freetown from 1808 to 1867 that hunted slave ships off West Africa after Britain banned the slave trade in 1807.
